AnalyzeResponse.description: A knowledge base built from documents alone. Nothing is stored.
AnalyzeResponse.title: AnalyzeResponse

CaseInvestigation.description:
A mission run in a case, with the outcome it reached (kept when the run ends, so a case still
knows its investigations after the engine restarts).
CaseInvestigation.title: CaseInvestigation

ChainEvidence.description: One citation in a finding's evidence chain (Phase 46).
ChainEvidence.title: ChainEvidence

ChainStep.description: One link from claim to conclusion, in order.
ChainStep.title: ChainStep

negation_check.default: not run: no verifier was given
negation_check.title: Negation Check

ClaimComparison.description: The temporal order of two claims.
ClaimComparison.title: ClaimComparison

ClaimConflict.description:
Two or more sources asserting different values for the same attribute of one entity.

Like the original, it never decides which side is right. It surfaces the disagreement with
every citation, and judging it is the reasoning engine's and the verifier's job.
ClaimConflict.title: ClaimConflict

ClaimElement.description:
One verifiable part of a claim.

Decomposition is what makes gaps specific. "The project slipped two weeks against the
approved baseline" contains a duration, a baseline and a comparison; checking support
per element is how the system can say *which* part is unsupported rather than shrugging
at the whole claim.
ClaimElement.title: ClaimElement

Confidence.description:
A computed confidence, inseparable from the inputs that produced it.

Constructed only via `Confidence.compute(...)`. The components travel with the value, so
any report, UI or evaluation can show *why* a number is what it is — and so a value that
looks wrong can be traced rather than argued about.
Confidence.title: Confidence

ConfidenceFactor.description:
One named input to a confidence (Phase 46), with what it contributed and why.

`contribution` is `weight * value` for a weighted factor, the multiplier's effect for the
resolution gate (weight 0), and minus the amount for a penalty. A factor that could not be
assessed has `assessed=False` and weight 0, and says why.
ConfidenceFactor.title: ConfidenceFactor

ConflictKind.description: How the conflicting values were compared. Reported so a reader knows what "differ" meant.
ConflictKind.title: ConflictKind

ConflictSide.description: One of the disagreeing values, with every claim and citation that asserts it.
ConflictSide.title: ConflictSide

CustodyAction.description: What can happen to evidence. A closed vocabulary, like every other in the system.
CustodyAction.title: CustodyAction

CustodyEvent.description: One link in the chain. Never updated, never deleted.
CustodyEvent.title: CustodyEvent

EntityInvestigation.description:
Everything known about one entity, in one response.

The original `/investigation/{name}` endpoint, which its README called the main one.
EntityInvestigation.title: EntityInvestigation

EntityNetwork.description: The neighbourhood of one entity, within `depth` hops in either direction.
EntityNetwork.title: EntityNetwork

EntityType.description: The original's six extraction types, plus OTHER for anything the model labels freely.
EntityType.title: EntityType

Episode.description:
One finding of one run, as Member 4 logged one question and answer.

Every finding is logged with its verification status, rejected ones included: a memory of
only what passed would make past investigations look better than they were.
Episode.title: Episode

EvidenceCitation.description: A finding that cited this evidence, from its CITED custody event.
EvidenceCitation.title: EvidenceCitation

EvidenceClassification.description: Handling sensitivity, set by a person. Enforced by access control in Phase 55.
EvidenceClassification.title: EvidenceClassification

EvidenceGap.description:
A specific missing piece of support, and what would close it.

`missing` is written for a human to read: it appears in the UI and in the report's
Limitations section. A gap that says "more evidence needed" has failed at its job.

missing.description: The specific absent element, e.g. 'approved baseline completion date'
missing.title: Missing

EvidenceGap.title: EvidenceGap

EvidenceRef.description:
A pointer from a claim to a source location.

Produced when a claim is made. Resolution happens afterwards, in the binder (Phase 13) —
which is precisely why `resolution` defaults to `UNRESOLVED`: nothing counts as resolved
until something has checked it.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

ExecutionSummary.description: What the run actually did. Every field is counted, never estimated.
ExecutionSummary.title: ExecutionSummary

ExtractionStats.description:
What building the knowledge base cost and what it could not do.

Counted, so a knowledge base built from half the documents can never look complete.
ExtractionStats.title: ExtractionStats

FactSupport.description: One run's citation of a fact: which investigation, and which line it read it from.
FactSupport.title: FactSupport

FactView.description: A fact as the API returns it, with its support count and runs as plain fields.
FactView.title: FactView

Finding.description: A structured claim, with everything needed to judge whether to believe it.
Finding.title: Finding

FindingChain.description:
How a finding came to be what it is: claim -> evidence -> extraction -> reasoning ->
verification -> conclusion, each step with what it rests on (Phase 46).
FindingChain.title: FindingChain

FindingClassification.description: How much epistemic weight a claim is entitled to.
FindingClassification.title: FindingClassification

FindingReview.description: A finding's review: whether it needs one and why, its state, and every decision.
FindingReview.title: FindingReview

FindingTrail.description: The subgraph a finding rests on: what lights up when a finding is clicked (A9).
FindingTrail.title: FindingTrail

FormatSpec.description: One family of file types: which extensions, which parser, and how it becomes text.
FormatSpec.title: FormatSpec

GapType.description: Why a claim element is unsupported. The type determines how to go and fix it.
GapType.title: GapType

GraphNode.description: One node. Entities are parents; their claims and documents are sub-nodes (`parent`).
GraphNode.title: GraphNode

HypothesisSet.description: The run's competing explanations, ranked by computed support, or why there are none.
HypothesisSet.title: HypothesisSet

InjectionScan.description:
What a scan of one untrusted text found.

A hit is not a verdict that the document is malicious. A security report quoting an attack
matches too. Hits are reported and the content is still read, as data, because dropping a
document on a pattern match would let an attacker delete evidence by quoting a phrase.
InjectionScan.title: InjectionScan

KnowledgeClaim.description: One source's assertion of one attribute value about one entity.
KnowledgeClaim.title: KnowledgeClaim

KnowledgeEntity.description: One real-world thing, resolved across every document that mentions it.
KnowledgeEntity.title: KnowledgeEntity

KnowledgeSnapshot.description:
A run's knowledge base. Built once per run and never shared between runs.

The original kept one SQLite file for every ingest ever made, so a later investigation saw
an earlier one's contradictions. Here the snapshot belongs to the run that built it.
KnowledgeSnapshot.title: KnowledgeSnapshot

KnownEntity.description: An entity as seen across investigations, merged by normalised name.
KnownEntity.title: KnownEntity

Lead.description: A line the next-evidence search found. A lead, not a finding: nothing has checked it.
Lead.title: Lead

Limitation.description:
Something that constrains how much the report can be trusted.

Generated from run facts — skipped tasks, unresolved gaps, degraded verification,
exhausted budget — not from the model's sense of modesty.
Limitation.title: Limitation

MetricPoint.description: One suite run, as a point on a trend line.
MetricPoint.title: MetricPoint

MissionDetail.description: A mission's current state, without the full event log.
MissionDetail.title: MissionDetail

MissionSummary.description: One row in the mission list.
MissionSummary.title: MissionSummary

NarrativeCheck.description:
Member 4's answer evaluation of one narrative paragraph (Phase 37).

Reports, never rewrites: the paragraph stays as written, and this sits beside it.
NarrativeCheck.title: NarrativeCheck

NodeDetail.description: Everything the hover pop-up and the side panel show for one node.
NodeDetail.title: NodeDetail

PartialDate.description:
A calendar date that may be missing its year or its day.

The original parsed with `strptime` and then forced every result to 2026 - including dates
that carried their own year, so "14 September 2025" became 2026. A partial date keeps what
the source actually said, and comparison treats an unknown field as unknown.
PartialDate.title: PartialDate

PlanChange.description: One "JARVIS changed its plan": what triggered it, why, and the plan before and after.
PlanChange.title: PlanChange

PlanStep.description: One task in the plan tree (Phase 49): why, what it took in, what it did, what came out.
PlanStep.title: PlanStep

PlanTree.description: Objective -> workstreams -> steps, and every change the run made to its plan (Phase 49).
PlanTree.title: PlanTree

ReportSection.description: One section. `narrative` is model-written; everything else is injected.
ReportSection.title: ReportSection

ResolutionStatus.description: Whether a citation was matched against content the system actually retrieved.
ResolutionStatus.title: ResolutionStatus

RetrievalHit.description: One passage, citable, with the score that ranked it.
RetrievalHit.title: RetrievalHit

SearchHit.description: A claim ranked by the original's explainable score. Every point has a reason.
SearchHit.title: SearchHit

SectionKind.description: The report's fixed structure. Order here is presentation order.
SectionKind.title: SectionKind

SentenceCheck.description: One sentence of the model-written narrative, judged against the report's evidence.
SentenceCheck.title: SentenceCheck

SimilarCase.description: Another case sharing indicators with this one (D19): context, never evidence.
SimilarCase.title: SimilarCase

SourceLocator.description:
Exactly where a piece of content came from.

This is what makes evidence checkable rather than decorative. "doc_A says the project
slipped" is an assertion; "project_report.pdf page 12, chars 400-520" is something a
reader can go and verify, and something the evidence binder can resolve against the
chunks actually retrieved.
SourceLocator.title: SourceLocator

Stage.description:
The phases a caller can show a progress indicator for.

Deliberately coarser than `EventType`: a user watching a run wants seven phases, not
thirty-nine event kinds. The event log remains the complete record.
Stage.title: Stage

StatementType.description:
What kind of statement a finding is (Phase 45), as a reader needs to know it.

Computed from the finding's evidence by `reasoning.statements.type_statement`, never taken from
the model: the model may propose a type, and the stricter of its proposal and the evidence wins.
`FindingClassification` stays the internal ruling that caps confidence; this is what is shown.
StatementType.title: StatementType

TaskType.description:
The closed vocabulary of task types.

A plan referencing a type outside this set fails validation (Phase 7). This is the
second half of the intent-vocabulary defence: operations the agent claims to need must
map to task types it can actually execute.
TaskType.title: TaskType

TimelineEvent.description: A dated claim, placed in order.
TimelineEvent.title: TimelineEvent

VerificationIssue.description:
One specific problem found with a claim.

Issues are the verifier's actual output. A bare status tells the replanning loop nothing
it can act on; `element` plus `issue_type` tells it exactly what to go and fix.
VerificationIssue.title: VerificationIssue

VerifierOpinion.description:
What one verifier said, when several were consulted for one verdict.

Recorded so disagreement between verifiers is measurable rather than resolved out of sight.
VerifierOpinion.title: VerifierOpinion

WorkingMemorySnapshot.description:
What a run had in mind when it finished: Member 4's `snapshot()`, read off the result.

Member 4 reduced evidence to a count in the snapshot; so does this.
WorkingMemorySnapshot.title: WorkingMemorySnapshot

app__api__v1__documents__StoredDocument.description: An earlier upload, offered again to a new mission.
app__api__v1__documents__StoredDocument.title: StoredDocument

app__intelligence__context__store__Store.description: A document as a workspace holds it.
app__intelligence__context__store__Store.title: StoredDocument

info.description:
An adaptive, evidence-driven investigation engine.

Missions run in the background: `POST /api/v1/missions` returns a run id immediately and
`GET /api/v1/missions/{id}/stream` streams the run as it happens. Every finding carries the
source locators it rests on, and every claim the evidence does not support is reported as
unsupported rather than dropped.
info.title: JARVIS

get.description: The audit log, newest first: every write the API received and the system's own actions.

schema.title: Response Get Audit Api V1 Audit Get

post.description: File existing evidence items in a case (from the locker, or another case).
Chunk, embed and store documents in a workspace. Unchanged files are not re-embedded.
The workspace's passages closest in meaning to the query, each a citation.

get.description: Every workspace that holds a document, and `default` always.

schema.title: Response Workspaces Api V1 Context Workspaces Get

get.description: A workspace's documents, with their parser, hash and chunk count.
Earlier uploads, newest first, so a new mission can reuse them without uploading again.

schema.title: Response List Uploads Api V1 Documents Get

post.description:
Store uploads and report what each one parsed as.

The response is the parse result, not an acknowledgement. A client that only learns a
file was accepted still does not know whether it will contribute anything to a run -
a 12-page scanned PDF with no text layer uploads perfectly and yields nothing.

schema.title: Response Upload Documents Api V1 Documents Post

get.description: Every file type a mission can read, which parser reads it, and how it becomes text.

schema.title: Response Formats Api V1 Documents Formats Get

get.description:
Which way is better for each metric.

Served rather than hardcoded in the UI: the direction of a metric is a property of the
metric, and a chart that colours a rising `unsupported_claim_rate` green because the
frontend held a stale copy of this list would be worse than no colour at all.

schema.title: Response Get Metric Directions Api V1 Evaluation Directions Get

get.description:
Every committed evaluation report, oldest first, as trend points.

Oldest first because this is charted as a series and a series reads left to right.

The UI must not join points across a change of `comparable_key`. Two reports produced with
different models or prompt versions describe different systems, and a line drawn between
them shows a regression or an improvement that never happened.

schema.title: Response Get Evaluation Reports Api V1 Evaluation Reports Get

get.description: Every evidence item, newest first. Uploads that predate the locker are registered here.
The source authority tiers an item can be given, highest first (Phase 45).

schema.title: Response Authority Tiers Api V1 Evidence Authority Get

get.description: The current item for a document name: the version a new mission naming it would read.

patch.description: Change what a person decides about an item. Recorded as METADATA_CHANGED, old and new.

schema.title: Response Get Custody Api V1 Evidence  Evidence Id  Custody Get

get.description: The stored original, byte for byte, under its original name.
The findings that cited this item, from its CITED custody events.

schema.title: Response Get Citations Api V1 Evidence  Evidence Id  Findings Get

post.description: Re-hash the stored original and, for the current version of a name, the working copy.

Member 3's standalone use: documents in, a knowledge base out, nothing stored.

The request waits for extraction, one model call per chunk, which is why the number of
documents is capped. Nothing is written to Neo4j: a knowledge base with no mission has no run
to belong to, and storing it would bring back the global store the port removed.

get.description: An entity as seen across investigations, with the facts known about it.
Episodes whose objective or claim contains `q`, newest first.

schema.title: Response Episodes Api V1 Memory Episodes Get

get.description: Facts by exact subject and predicate (normalised), best supported first.

schema.title: Response Facts Api V1 Memory Facts Get

delete.description:
Remove what one mission contributed to memory: its episodes, its archived snapshot, its
support for facts. A fact or entity nothing else supports goes with it; one other missions also
saw stays, with their support. The mission itself and its recording are untouched.

schema.title: Response List Missions Api V1 Missions Get

post.description: Start a mission. 202, not 201: the work is accepted, not finished.

Ask a mission to stop. 202: cancellation is cooperative, so it is requested, not done.

The run stops at its next await point - a tool call or model call boundary - and keeps
whatever it had already established.

get.description: Every challenge made of this run's findings, latest per finding (Phase 48).

schema.title: Response Get Challenges Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Challenges Get

get.description: The full event log, paginated. This is the run's reconstructable record.

From claim to conclusion (Phase 46): each citation with its evidence item, authority, line
text and what was extracted from it; how reasoning proposed it; what each verifier said; and
the confidence with its factors.

post.description:
Challenge one finding (Phase 48): look for counter-evidence in the run's documents, check
its own lines, verify it against the counter lines with the configured verifier, weigh
authority, and recompute its confidence. The finding itself is not changed; the challenge is
kept beside it, with who asked.

Decide on a finding. REJECTED and MODIFIED need a reason; MODIFIED the reworded claim. Each
decision is a new record - a changed mind does not erase the first.

get.description: The claims, documents and entities a finding rests on (A9).

schema.title: Response Get Gaps Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Gaps Get

get.description:
The competing explanations, ranked by computed support, with what would decide each and
where to look next (Phase 47). Empty with a reason when the objective asked for none.

The report as it stands now: findings with their reviews and challenges, evidence with hashes
and integrity, timeline, contradictions, explanations, unknowns, recommendations, trace.

Download the report as md, pdf, docx or json. Recorded: a REPORTED custody event on every
cited evidence item, and an audit entry carrying the content hash.

schema.title: Response Claims Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Claims Get
Response Conflicts Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Conflicts Get

get.description: The same attribute described in other words (BUG-033): shown, never a contradiction.

schema.title: Response Differences Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Differences Get
Response Entities Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Entities Get

get.description: Nodes and links for the 3D explorer: everything, or `focus`'s neighbourhood.
What the hover pop-up shows for one node.

schema.title: Response Relationships Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Relationships Get
Response Search Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Search Get
Response Timeline Api V1 Missions  Run Id  Knowledge Timeline Get

get.description:
The plan as a person reads it (Phase 49): objective, workstreams, and each step's why,
inputs, action, output, dependencies and status; then every change the run made, and why.
The same report a human reads, as Markdown.
Every finding of a run: whether it needs review and why, its state and its decisions.
Server-sent events for a running mission. See ADR-008.
The task graph with live statuses, plus the waves that can run concurrently.
Recorded runs available to replay, newest first.

schema.title: Response Get Recordings Api V1 Recordings Get

get.description:
One recording: its events and the run's final state.

Served whole. A replay needs every event in order, and paginating them would make the
client reassemble a file that is already a single document.

schema.title: Response Get Recording Api V1 Recordings  Name  Get

get.description: Whether the engine can actually run. Reports the model, not just a 200.
